one_month_reasoning: Inside the window: Q3 2026 results and the rolled-forward 2027-2031 capital plan, financing plan and EPS outlook on Oct 29 (source 25); the MPUC response to the reconsideration petitions on the 9.6% ROE (deadline Oct 19, source 11) and early reaction to NSPM's proposed 2027-28 base-rate freeze (source 6); the 10-yr Treasury, which has risen from 4.00% to 5.12% in a year (source 19) and drives the group P/E; and Anthropic IPO supply (source 17), which competes for AI-themed money more than for the utility income base. The plan update is two-sided: a larger plan (6 GW data-center target, $10B+ line of sight) lifts rate-base growth but brings more equity (40% of incremental capex) and possibly a lower 2027 starting point under the MN freeze. No strong directional edge, so the ladder is a near-symmetric lognormal around $76.9 with monthly vol ~5.4% (19%/3.5) and a 10% weight on a 10% vol component for the plan/earnings event.

fair_value.method: Engine blend: P/E 17.0x on rate-base NTM EPS $4.85 at the horizon = $82.3 (w 0.8) and driver DCF at 5.87% WACC / 4% terminal = $50.5 (w 0.2, per forward-P/E table), less a probability-weighted Texas wildfire claim; dividend-discount cross-check $74.5.

methods.name: DCF

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The discount has persisted since the 2024 Smokehouse Creek fire and is structural through the horizon: (1) wildfire liability with no Colorado liability shield enacted (Bill 5 draft only) and an open Texas AG suit; (2) the heaviest equity need in the group ($7B base plan, 69.7M forward shares outstanding) diluting EPS growth below 11% rate-base growth; (3) PSCo's 13-month historical test year and 9.3% ROE vs 9.8% asked, plus NSPM's proposed 2027-28 base-rate freeze, which signal affordability pressure and lag. Offsetting: top-quartile 9%+ EPS growth and contracted data-center load, so I do not use a deeper discount.

thesis_break_reason: $63 is ~18% below today, below the 52-week low ($68.72) and ~13x NTM EPS, under every peer but ES. Absent a market-wide crash, that level would most likely mean something fundamental: a new utility-ignited wildfire with multi-billion liability, a capital plan cut or failure of the Google/Colorado data-center approvals, a ratings-driven equity raise well above the $7B plan, or regulators forcing earned ROE toward 8%.

reverse_dcf_check: Engine: the P/E leg ($82.3) implies a WACC of 5.5% with 4% terminal growth and my 2026-30 driver path; my CAPM WACC is 5.87% and gives $50.5. Put differently, 17x NTM EPS implies the market expects ~9% EPS growth through ~2031 and ~4% after, with ROE held at ~9%; plausible given the contracted data-center load and an 11% rate-base CAGR, but only if allowed ROEs hold near 9.3-9.6% and equity needs stay near 40% of incremental capex. The ~$9/share probability-weighted long-dated risks above are already inside the 1.85-turn discount to the peer median (1.85 x $4.85 = ~$9).

sbc_treatment.note: SBC $46M in FY2025 (F36), ~0.3% of revenue; ongoing EPS and GAAP EBIT are after SBC, peers' consensus EPS likewise; share count grows by forward-equity settlements, not by SBC.

reasoning: Industry/regulatory read: (1) Demand: XEL has ~2 GW of data centers operating, under construction or under ESA (Utility Dive), targets 6 GW contracted by end-2027 (TIKR), and Google's Pine Island ESA with 1,900 MW of clean resources is pending (decision early 2027) with Google paying the cost of new service (10-Q). The project's AI-capex standing view has base customer capex rising $1.2T->$1.8T->$2.3T in 2026-28, and the WSJ's report of Anthropic's draft S-1 (~$450B of mostly noncancelable cloud commitments to Google, AWS, Microsoft, plus $86B with Nscale/Lambda) is a general positive demand signal; I found no named source tying Anthropic to a site in XEL's territory (Anthropic's Fluidstack sites are in Texas and New York, unnamed; no link to SPS). Counterparty risk: MN's approved tariff (>100 MW, 15-yr minimum, minimum bills, exit fees, credit requirements) and CO's proposed tariff (>50 MW, 80% take, 6-month deposit, exit fee = remaining minimum bills) push stranded-cost risk onto customers and collateral; the gap is SPS (TX/NM tariffs only to be filed by end-2026), where Fermi America's 200 MW ESA lost its tenant in Dec 2025 - small (≈10% of contracted load). Backlash: Anthropic's own risk factor about organised opposition is visible in MN (statewide moratorium bill pushed by opponents, Elk River council rejecting a data-center rule change), a risk to the 6 GW upside rather than the base plan. (2) Regulation: MN ROE 9.25%->9.6% but under AG reconsideration, and NSPM now proposes a 2027-28 base-rate freeze (offset by ITC acceleration): an affordability signal; PSCo got $157M of $356M at 9.3% on a historical test year. (3) Rates: 10-yr 5.12% (+112bp y/y) explains the -5.5% year despite +8% EPS growth. Valuation: rate-base EPS build $4.51 FY2027 (consensus $4.54) and $4.85 NTM at the horizon x 17x (10% discount to the 18.85x peer median, justified by wildfire, equity needs, lag) = $82.3; DCF $50.5 at 5.87% WACC (sector-wide gap, explained); engine blend $75.96. Ladder: the 12-month price follows the group P/E and today's price more than the DCF, so I centre the mixture at ~$79 (bear $66 25% incl. 3% wildfire tail ~$52, base $79 50%, bull $92 25%, within-scenario vol ~12%), giving median ~$78.7 and an overall spread a bit below the 19% realised vol because regulated EPS is visible. Anthropic IPO / liquidity: utilities' income holders overlap little with IPO buyers, but the AI-power sleeve of XEL's holder base could be trimmed around the pricing; a move toward $70 without a change in rate-base EPS or the 10-yr would put XEL at ~14.5x NTM and is the kind of drawdown I would treat as a buying opportunity; below $63 (thesis break) re-check wildfire/regulatory news first. Research limits: X/Twitter not used; MN Reformer and Axios blocked fetches (used MPR instead); Colorado large-load tariff decision not yet issued.

model_inputs.dcf_check: DCF $50.5 is 39% below the P/E leg ($82.3). Cause: at a CAPM WACC of 5.87% and allowed returns close to that (after-tax return on rate base ~7.0%), a regulated asset is worth about its rate base (EV at horizon ~1.0-1.1x RB of ~$75B) less ~$48B net debt; the market pays ~1.3x rate base (EV $85B vs 2026 RB $66B) because it capitalises utility earnings at an implied WACC of ~5.5% (engine reverse DCF). The gap is sector-wide (peers at 18.85x would show the same), not XEL-specific, so I keep the DCF at its table weight as a valuation anchor and do not move the P/E.
